questions.stem: A 35-year-old came to Medicine OPD with complaints of lethargy, weight gain, and increased sleep. Investigations were done which revealed low TSH plasma concentration however, on administration of TRH, TSH was increased which of the following is likely to be present?

options.label: C
options.text: Hypothyroidism due to disease in pituitary

options.label: D
options.text: Hypothyroidism due to disease in the hypothalamus

questions.answerText: Hypothyroidism due to disease in the hypothalamus
questions.solutionHtml:

questions.stem: A 29-year-old lady is diagnosed with Hashimoto thyroiditis and a positive antibody titer against thyroid oxidase enzyme. Which of the following is not a function of the affected enzyme?
questions.solutionHtml:
Iodide trapping

lodide trapping (iodide uptake) is not catalyzed by thyroid peroxidase. Oxidation, organification, and coupling are catalyzed by it.




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no. 951, 952, and 953

questions.stem: Jitendra, a resident of Rajasthan present with hyperthyroidism and is planning for thyroidectomy. To achieve a euthyroid status preoperatively, he started on Lugol's iodine solution. Which of the following best describes its mechanism of action?

options.label: D
options.text: Inhibition of organification and synthesis of thyroid hormones

questions.answerText: Inhibition of organification and synthesis of thyroid hormones
questions.solutionHtml:
Inhibition of organification and synthesis of thyroid hormones

The introduction of exogenous iodine in the form of Lugol's iodine solution leads to transient inhibition of organification and synthesis of thyroid hormones. This is known as the Wolff-chaikoff effect.




Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no 365

questions.stem: Which of the following is false regarding thyroid hormone?

options.label: A
options.text: T3 is more avidly bound to nuclear receptors than T4

options.label: C
options.text: T3 is more active than T4

options.label: D
options.text: T4 has a shorter half-life than T3

questions.answerText: T4 has a shorter half-life than T3
questions.solutionHtml:
T4 has a shorter half-life than T3

T4 doesn't have a shorter half-life than T3, rather T3 has a shorter half-life and more rapid action than T4.




Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page no 359

questions.stem: Jitendra, a 15-year-old adolescent, is suspected of having anorexia nervosa. Thyroid function tests are also drawn. His TSH is in the normal range, but the rT3 level is elevated. Which of the following is the most accurate statement regarding her status?

options.label: A
options.text: Reverse T3 has no biological effect

options.label: B
options.text: This patient probably has T3 thyroiditis

options.label: C
options.text: The free rT3 would be the next step to assess possible hyperthyroidism

questions.answerText: Reverse T3 has no biological effect
questions.solutionHtml:
Reverse T3 has no biological effect
  • Reverse T3 has no biological effect. Individuals with anorexia nervosa often have an increased rT3 level and a lower T3 level, reflecting a lower metabolism rate as compensation for the markedly decreased caloric intake.
  • The fact that hisTSH is in the normal range makes it difficult to make a diagnosis of hypothyroidism.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no. 944

questions.stem: A 41-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician with weight and hair loss, diarrhea, nervousness, and eye pressure. She has no medical problems, but some of her family members have similar symptoms and require medication. On examination, she is noted to have exophthalmos, an enlarged non tender goiter, hyperreflexia, and tremor when her arms are outstretched. The patient has a decreased thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) level and an increased free thyroxine (T4) level. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Graves disease
  • The patient has a decreased thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) level and an increased free thyroxine (T4) level and is diagnosed with Graves disease (hyperthyroidism).
  • Clue in this case:- woman has weight and hair loss, diarrhea, nervousness, eye pressure, nontender goiter, exophthalmos, and laboratory evidence of hyperthyroidism.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no 944.

questions.stem: A 43-year-old female complains of weight loss, hyperhidrosis, low-grade fever, and increased irritability. She has been found to have hyperfunction of the sympathetic-adrenal system and basal metabolism. These disorders can be caused by hypersecretion of the following hormone?
questions.solutionHtml:
Thyroxine

The complaints of that patient – weight loss, hyperhidrosis, low-grade fever, increased

irritability, and the increase in basal metabolic rate are the symptoms of hypersecretion of thyroid hormones (hyperthyroidism).




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no 944.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old pregnant woman and her 3-year-old child are seen in a medical camp in Himachal Pradesh. The child is short in stature, has a potbelly, enlarged protruding tongue, and is developmentally delayed. Iodine is prescribed for mother and child, with the hope of preventing mental retardation in the developing fetus. Iodides are stored in the thyroid follicles mainly in the form of which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Thyroglobulin

The thyroid gland stores iodide primarily as thyroglobulin.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.861.

questions.stem: All the following are functions of thyroid cells except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Synthesises thyroid hormones

Thyroid hormone synthesis takes place in the follicular cells of the thyroid gland. The whole process involves an intact and coordinated synthesis pathway containing sodium iodide symporter (NIS), thyroperoxidase (TPO), thyroglobulin, and adequate dietary iodide.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 304.

questions.stem: In the thyroid, ‘coupling reaction’ forms all the following except:
questions.solutionHtml:
DIT

In Coupling reactions T3, T4 and rT3 form with the help of MIT and DIT.

Coupling reactions: TPO combines iodinated tyrosine residues to make MIT + DIT = T3 (triiodothyronine). DIT + DIT = T4 (tetraiodothyronine)




Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Page Number: 953.
